claims.text: A DNN potential can describe (TiZrTaHfNb)C0.75N0.25 in both crystalline and liquid states near its melting point.
(TiZrTaHfNb)C0.75N0.25 has a melting temperature in the approximate range 3500–3600 K.
The proposed DNN reference would be trained on extensive ab initio sampling of liquid configurations.
Replacing an EAM reference with a liquid-trained DNN reference will improve reference–target phase-space overlap in thermodynamic integration.
The proposed method applies to near-equiatomic multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their high melting temperatures.
High-entropy alloys generally contain more than four metallic components in near-equiatomic proportions with chemical disorder.
A DNN potential maps diverse atomic configurations through many-body interaction modeling.
The DNN bridges the representational gap between an EAM reference and the ab initio liquid target.
A DNN trained on comprehensive ab initio molecular-dynamics configurations more accurately represents heterogeneous bonding and local structural fluctuations in the liquid.
Improved representation of liquid bonding and structural fluctuations increases overlap with the ab initio target phase space.
Improved phase-space overlap produces a smoother thermodynamic-integration path with fewer mismatches than an EAM reference.
The DNN reference may reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 30–50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM reference.
TOR-TILD's EAM references inadequately represent the diverse atomic configurations of an ab initio multicomponent liquid.
The benefit of the DNN reference will diminish in elemental or binary systems and at lower temperatures because EAM potentials may already capture the relevant physics there.
The quantitative improvement depends on the range and quality of the ab initio training set, DNN architecture, and alloy system.
